summary: newWorkflowArchiveCmd (internal/cli/channel_workflow.go) constructs a real `sync` command instance (newSyncCmd(flags)) with --resources workouts,classes (which cascades to performance/workout_details) plus its own --db/--full/--max-parents/--stale-before flags translated into sync args, and executes it via ExecuteContext rather than re-implementing sync's resource list, dependent fan-out, or bounding logic. It sets SilenceErrors/SilenceUsage on the detached sync instance so a failure doesn't print twice (once from the detached command's own Execute(), once when its error propagates back to the real root's Execute()). Any future change to sync's resource list, dependent cascade, or bounding semantics is automatically inherited here -- workflow_archive must keep delegating, never grow a second hand-rolled sync loop, or these two commands will silently diverge again.
reason: newWorkflowArchiveCmd's resource list was hardcoded to an empty slice (`resources := []string{}`), so every invocation -- with or without --full, --dry-run, or any flag -- silently reported {"resources_synced":0,"total_items":0} and archived nothing at all, on any account, confirmed live. This is also reachable as an MCP tool (`workflow` is one of the framework tool groups), so an agent calling it saw a clean success response for a command that never did anything. A round-9 report characterized this as "no bounding flags, same as pre-round-4 sync" and suggested adding --max-parents/--stale-before; investigation found the command was actually non-functional altogether, a materially worse defect than reported, which a minimal flag-only fix wouldn't have caught. User chose full delegation to sync's proven machinery over a second hand-rolled bounded loop or redirecting the command to fail with a pointer to sync.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. TestWorkflowArchiveActuallyArchivesData drives the real command end-to-end against a fake server and asserts all four cascaded resources (workouts, classes, performance, workout_details) end up populated, and that --json output matches sync's own event-stream shape rather than the old dead-command shape. TestWorkflowArchiveBoundingFlagsAccepted confirms --max-parents/--stale-before are real, wired flags. Live-verified against the real account with --max-parents 5: all four resources reported success=4/warned=0/errored=0 (workouts synced, classes fully paginated at 48,742 items in ~4.5 minutes -- classes has no incremental filter so this cost is inherent to the account/API, not introduced by this fix -- and performance/workout_details each correctly capped at "processed 5 of 3582 pending parents this call; 3577 remain"), where every previous invocation reported 0 synced regardless of flags.
